stories.headline: Northflank breach exposes customer AI API keys
stories.technical: Northflank disclosed a breach after Wiz alerted it on 30 October. Attackers abused customer AI API keys; stored environment variables may have been decrypted and secrets stolen. The platform patched network policies and enabled credential rotation for PostgreSQL, MongoDB, MySQL and Redis. Initial access remains undisclosed, and the number of affected customers is unknown.
stories.why_it_matters: Rotate all Northflank secrets and review AI provider billing logs for unauthorised usage.

stories.headline: Reddit to require logins to restrict content scraping
stories.technical: Reddit will pilot requiring accounts for full content access in selected markets outside the United States, while keeping front pages and linked pages visible. The platform says logged-out pages enable most unauthorised data access. It will continue licensing data to AI platforms and search engines, and plans a read-only incognito mode plus personalised advertising opt-out.
stories.why_it_matters: Expect reduced anonymous browsing and more account-based tracking; review privacy settings and opt out where available.

stories.headline: Microsoft fixes 3 high severity Chromium flaws in Edge
stories.technical: Microsoft has released three high severity security fixes for Edge, incorporating upstream Chromium patches. The update addresses a use-after-free vulnerability in the video component tracked as CVE-2026-118313, an improper input validation flaw in SVG handling tracked as CVE-2026-118315, and a memory corruption vulnerability within the Paint component tracked as CVE-2026-118312.
stories.why_it_matters: Apply the current browser updates through your vendor release channel.

stories.headline: VOLTA infostealer uses AI to prioritise victims for monetisation
stories.technical: CAIRN research identifies VOLTA-AUTODOXER, a self-deleting Windows infostealer. It steals browser credentials, cookies, payment cards, wallet seed phrases, messaging sessions, OAuth tokens, SSH and cloud keys, then sends a victim dossier to OpenRouter for LLM-based asset valuation. It falls back across up to three models when refusals occur.
stories.why_it_matters: Treat stolen sessions, OAuth tokens and cloud keys as high priority; revoke sessions and rotate credentials.

stories.headline: Romance scam defendants pleaded guilty to $9m wire fraud
stories.technical: Three defendants pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit wire fraud over a romance scam targeting elderly victims. Jamal and Kamal Abubakari and Amanda Joy Opoku-Boachie were arrested in Virginia in May 2026. Investigators said the victims believed they had found romantic partners before their savings were depleted, with proceeds used to buy jewellery and a Lamborghini.
stories.why_it_matters: Treat unexpected romance approaches as scams and never send money or financial details.

stories.headline: Lapsus$ teen hacking group claims Okta and Microsoft breaches
stories.technical: Four years ago, the Lapsus$ group posted screenshots claiming they had accessed the identity provider Okta and Microsoft's source code. They used bribed insiders, SIM swaps and MFA fatigue rather than advanced malware to get inside. Several members, including teenagers from the UK, were later arrested.
stories.why_it_matters: Simple social engineering beat some of the world's biggest companies.

stories.headline: Delete accounts you no longer use
stories.technical: Old accounts on forums, shops and apps still hold your details, and often an old reused password. When those sites are breached, your data goes with them. Close what you don't need and change the password on anything you keep.
stories.why_it_matters: Every unused account is a breach waiting to include you.

stories.headline: Modern account takeover threats bypass traditional password security
stories.technical: Identity thieves are increasingly exploiting session cookies, SIM swapping techniques, and multi-factor authentication fatigue to bypass standard password-based login security controls, enabling unauthorized account takeovers without requiring credential theft.
stories.why_it_matters: Review MFA configurations and monitor for session cookie theft.

stories.headline: Ransomware as accepted as COVID-19
stories.technical: Ransomware-as-a-Service (RaaS) enables anonymous criminal groups to profit from attacks. Victims face social backlash, similar to COVID-19 self-responsibility theories.
stories.why_it_matters: Understand the societal impact of ransomware

stories.headline: Floin AG reportedly offline after alleged cyberattack
stories.technical: Floin AG, a Liechtenstein MiCA-licensed crypto platform, reportedly went offline after a cyberattack. The claim remains unconfirmed: no company statement, regulator notice, affected system, user count, loss figure or ransom demand has been identified.
stories.why_it_matters: Check Floin account status and avoid acting on unverified outage claims.

stories.headline: ChatGPT shared link can run attacker code and read chats
stories.technical: A malicious shared ChatGPT link can execute code inside a logged‑in session, read private conversations and exfiltrate data. The flaw uses the Preview feature, MathLive library, and a YouTube‑hosted script to bypass CSP. OpenAI rated it P1 and patched it eight days after disclosure.
stories.why_it_matters: Patch OpenAI ChatGPT shared link handling immediately to stop code execution.

stories.headline: Seminole County Clerk services disrupted by cyberattack
stories.technical: The Seminole County Clerk of Court reported a cyberattack affecting its website and phone systems. The office disconnected external internet access during its investigation and found no ransomware or confirmed compromised information. Services were limited, with only cash and cheque payments accepted. The incident is separate from Florida Department of Education financial-aid website breach reports.
stories.why_it_matters: Check court service availability and payment options before visiting; no confirmed data theft reported.

stories.headline: Man impersonated woman to claim £172,000 in DWP benefits
stories.technical: Atikur Rahman used a false identity to claim Universal Credit, Maternity Allowance, Tax Credits and Child Benefit, obtaining approximately £172,000. The case illustrates identity fraud and benefit abuse targeting UK welfare systems.
stories.why_it_matters: Report suspicious benefit identity claims and strengthen identity verification for maternity and family payments.

stories.headline: NPC Investigates Data Breach of Overseas Employment Systems
stories.technical: The National Privacy Commission (NPC) is investigating a data breach affecting the Philippine Overseas Employment Administration's systems. Cybersecurity firm Hunt.io recovered file names related to the breach, but the status of the 69GB of data is unknown.
stories.why_it_matters: Check if your data was affected and stay informed about the investigation

stories.headline: Chainalysis breach exposes customer details via offensive agentic techniques
stories.technical: Blockchain analytics company Chainalysis confirmed a cyberattack in October 2026 involving offensive agentic techniques. Attackers accessed internal systems and exposed customer user IDs, full names, email addresses, and organisation roles. Chainalysis stated that no investigation records, passwords, MFA secrets, or session tokens were compromised. External experts were engaged, and platform vulnerabilities were patched.
stories.why_it_matters: Be alert for targeted phishing using exposed employee names, emails, and role labels.

stories.headline: Blossom Health breach exposes medical and insurance data
stories.technical: Blossom BH Opco Inc., trading as Blossom Health, reported a breach affecting 27,623 individuals, including names, medical information and health insurance data. The Texas Attorney General filing confirms the incident. DataBreaches.net reported that Stuckin2019 sent an extortion message through a purported clinician account, alleging access via an old staging environment and demanding $30,000 in Bitcoin. The company had not publicly confirmed the attacker’s claims.
stories.why_it_matters: Review medical records and benefit statements, and consider a credit freeze or fraud alert.

stories.headline: TikTok Pro fake app scams target Android and iPhone users
stories.technical: Malicious Android apps impersonating TikTok Pro spread through SMS and chat links, bypassing official app stores. Tapping links downloads APK files and prompts users to permit installation from unknown sources. Documented permissions included camera access. iPhone versions were delivered through links, profiles and account scams rather than app stores.
stories.why_it_matters: Install TikTok only from official stores and reject messages offering a Pro edition.

stories.headline: OneDrive URLs expose usernames despite Microsoft’s low-risk assessment
stories.technical: OneDrive and SharePoint URLs can reveal user principal names for organisational accounts without authentication. Microsoft classifies this as passive reconnaissance, not account compromise. Standard sign-in logs and Microsoft Purview do not record URL probing, while automatic throttling limits but does not prevent enumeration. Discovered usernames could support phishing, brute-force, credential stuffing and social engineering.
stories.why_it_matters: Monitor for suspicious URL probing and enforce phishing-resistant authentication to reduce account-takeover risk.

stories.headline: Cookie theft scam gives attackers digital keys to accounts
stories.technical: NCSC warns that attackers can steal session cookies via malware delivered through AiTM phishing. The malware harvests browser cookie stores, enabling account takeover. Affected browsers include Chrome, Firefox and Edge. No CVE IDs are cited. Keep OS and browsers updated and use a VPN.
stories.why_it_matters: Log out after use and keep software updated to stop cookie theft

stories.headline: CEO Fraud Scams Target Finance Teams
stories.technical: Criminals impersonate executives via email, WhatsApp, or calls, exploiting workplace hierarchies. They gather info from LinkedIn and company websites, then send urgent payment requests. Employees are discouraged from verifying requests due to claimed sensitivity.
stories.why_it_matters: Verify requests with a second channel

stories.headline: Microsoft says 99% of account attacks use stolen credentials
stories.technical: Microsoft’s Digital Defense Report 2025 analysed 100 trillion security signals daily and observed about 600 million account-targeting attacks daily. Over 99% were password-based, with Microsoft blocking 7,000 password attacks per second. Attackers use credentials exposed through phishing and breaches, alongside cybercrime-as-a-service operations, rather than exploiting systems directly.
stories.why_it_matters: Use unique passwords and multi-factor authentication to stop stolen-credential account takeovers.

stories.headline: AI-generated code security improves, but complex flaws persist
stories.technical: Veracode researchers analysed 18 frontier AI models across four programming languages. Overall vulnerability rates fell from 44% to 38%, while the security score rose from 56% to 62%. Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6-Sol scored 73%. Models still struggled with complex data-flow reasoning, including log injection prevention, and failed more than one in four security tasks.
stories.why_it_matters: Test AI-generated code independently before deployment; improving models still miss complex vulnerabilities.

stories.headline: Nine AI Platforms Hit by 'Black October' Attack Wave
stories.technical: In October, nine AI developer platforms reported attacks. Credential theft, privilege escalation, and third‑party vendor dependencies were common vectors. The attacks included agent swarm tactics, distillation attempts, and LLMJacking. A supply‑chain breach linked to the Mini‑Shai Hulud campaign also impacted Lightning. No CVE IDs were disclosed.
stories.why_it_matters: Patch or secure credentials on AI platforms immediately.

stories.headline: Saga University ransomware incident may expose 80,000 records
stories.technical: Saga University confirmed ransomware damage to an administrative file storage device in September 2026. The university reported possible external leakage of personal information for approximately 80,000 students and staff, plus patient information from an affiliated hospital. The incident illustrates double-extortion risk, where stolen data remains exposed even if backups restore encrypted files.
stories.why_it_matters: Check whether your data was affected and monitor for misuse linked to the university or hospital.

stories.headline: Young Australian loses bank balance in minutes to convincing scam
stories.technical: A young Australian reported seeing her entire bank account drained within minutes after falling for a convincing scam. The excerpt does not identify the initial contact method, payment mechanism, malicious infrastructure, affected bank, or any technical indicators.
stories.why_it_matters: Treat unexpected bank calls and payment requests sceptically; contact your bank directly if money disappears.

stories.headline: Applebee’s fixes app flaw exposing customer database
stories.technical: A hardcoded database credential in Applebee’s Android app allowed unauthorised access to customer records. Exposed fields included names, email addresses, dates of birth, phone numbers, ZIP codes, veteran status, login counts, account creation dates and recent login IP addresses. The credential could also permit modification of customer data. The flaw was fixed after disclosure.
stories.why_it_matters: Applebee’s customers should watch for phishing and monitor accounts for misuse of exposed personal details.

stories.headline: Yoba malware uses fake AI projects to mine cryptocurrency
stories.technical: Check Point Research tracked Yoba campaigns using fake GitHub AI applications, including GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus. ZIP releases contain signed OpenAI or Anthropic Setup.exe binaries alongside malicious winmm.dll files loaded through DLL sideloading. YobaDropper launches YobaLoader, which contacts attacker infrastructure and retrieves the final cryptocurrency-mining payload.
stories.why_it_matters: Avoid downloading purported AI tools from GitHub; verify repositories and scan ZIP files before execution.

stories.headline: UK specialist develops open-source tool to detect software supply-chain risks
stories.technical: UK-based cybersecurity specialist Adebayo Aderibigbe has released LeetGuard, an open-source security scanner designed to identify hidden risks in third-party software dependencies. Unlike conventional tools that rely solely on known vulnerability databases, LeetGuard evaluates code maintenance health and static package inspection to spot unmaintained libraries and structural decay, mapping findings to ISO/IEC 27001 compliance frameworks.
stories.why_it_matters: Use LeetGuard to identify unmaintained open-source software dependencies and automate supply-chain compliance.

stories.headline: DOJ seeks privacy safeguards for Character.AI chat data sale
stories.technical: Character.AI’s bankruptcy has prompted DOJ to seek an ombudsman and tighter court oversight over sale of chats and PII. The policy permits PII disclosure during asset sales, despite chatbot assurances of confidentiality; 12 million monthly users are affected.
stories.why_it_matters: Users should review privacy settings and avoid sharing sensitive personal information with chatbots.

stories.headline: AI guardrail refusals reveal hidden code vulnerabilities
stories.technical: CrowdStrike’s Guardrail-based Vulnerability Discovery (GbVD) method treats frontier-model refusals as signals of dangerous code. In controlled tests across five vulnerability classes, it identified 73 of 86 scenarios correctly and found undisclosed flaws in open-source projects. The study also suggests bisection can localise suspicious code by measuring response changes.
stories.why_it_matters: Treat unexplained AI refusals as leads, then manually verify and responsibly disclose suspicious code.

stories.headline: CrowdStrike expands prompt injection taxonomy for agent planning attacks
stories.technical: CrowdStrike AI security researchers updated their public Prompt Injection Taxonomy to 222 techniques, adding methods targeting autonomous agents’ planning and reasoning. The research describes indirect prompt injection where manipulated test utilities instruct coding agents to collect local configuration, including credentials, and submit them to an external diagnostics endpoint.
stories.why_it_matters: Secure agent workflows holistically, including planning context, tool use and data exfiltration paths.

stories.headline: Spotting False Claims and Online Scams on Social Media
stories.technical: Social media posts often embed malicious links that redirect to spoofed sites designed to harvest credentials. Attackers use convincing copy, fake government or aid claims, and social engineering to trick users into entering personal data. The tactics rely on trust and urgency, not technical exploits.
stories.why_it_matters: Avoid clicking suspicious links and verify sources before sharing

stories.headline: PHP2Shell Vulnerability Exposes 36M Sites, Threatens Firewalls
stories.technical: CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, a 9.2 CVSS PHP flaw, exposed 36.7 million services and 1.3‑1.9 million vulnerable hosts. 73% of 167 million PHP packages were internet‑facing. PAN‑OS firewalls were the first 25 servers hit, prompting an NSA warning to pull the plug.
stories.why_it_matters: Patch PHP and PAN‑OS immediately to stop remote code execution.

stories.headline: n0n ransomware group exposed while using AI and stolen credentials
stories.technical: The n0n ransomware operator targeted organizations across 14 countries using stolen credentials, weak passwords, exposed RDP, FortiGate VPN portals, and AWS access keys rather than zero-days. The attacker spent over $7,000 on AI coding agents, including OpenCode and various LLMs, to write and debug scripts. Victims suffered data theft, encryption, and deletion of backups.
stories.why_it_matters: Ensure MFA is enforced, audit cloud access keys, and secure RDP and VPN portals.

stories.headline: Warhorse Studios Hit by Cyberattack
stories.technical: Warhorse Studios, developer of Kingdom Come: Deliverance, suffered a cyberattack resulting in unauthorized access to its internal systems. The extent of the breach is still under investigation, with personal data potentially compromised.
stories.why_it_matters: Check if you're affected, change passwords if necessary

stories.headline: Fashion retailer Revolve reports theft of customer payment card data
stories.technical: Online retailer Revolve disclosed a cyber incident involving unauthorised access to multiple internal systems. Threat actors used automated methods to extract names, contact details, and payment card information from customers with saved account details. Over 128,000 victims have been identified across Texas and Vermont, with further breach notifications filed in Massachusetts.
stories.why_it_matters: Monitor accounts for fraudulent activity if you have a saved card on Revolve.

stories.headline: Android 17 reaches 1% adoption as older versions persist
stories.technical: Android Studio data reported by heise.de indicates Android 17 runs on 1% of active devices, while Android 16 holds 25.4%. Android 14 accounts for 15%, Android 15 14.7%, Android 13 11.8%, Android 11 10.1% and Android 12 nearly 10%. About 40% of devices remain on Android 13 or earlier.
stories.why_it_matters: Update eligible devices promptly to reduce exposure to known Android vulnerabilities.

The messages claim recipients have unpaid traffic summonses or parking fines and include malicious links. These links lead to fraudulent web portals designed to harvest personal information, credit card details, and online banking credentials through impersonation of official payment platforms.
stories.why_it_matters: Do not click links in SMS messages regarding traffic fines; use official portals instead.

stories.headline: Apple warns of mercenary spyware infections in 99 countries
stories.technical: Apple sent targeted mercenary spyware infection notifications to users in 99 countries, including journalists and documentary filmmakers. The company has notified more than 150 countries cumulatively but does not attribute attacks to specific threat actors or regions. Researchers recommend enabling Lockdown Mode and contacting Access Now; absence of a notification does not exclude infection.
stories.why_it_matters: Enable Lockdown Mode and seek specialist support if you receive an Apple threat notification.

stories.headline: Hackers steal 1.5 billion dollars in Ethereum from Bybit exchange
stories.technical: Attackers compromised Safe{Wallet}, a third-party multi-signature wallet platform used by Bybit cryptocurrency exchange. By inserting malicious code into the wallet-signing interface, the attackers altered transaction screens. Authorised signatories unknowingly approved a transfer of 401,000 Ether to attacker-controlled addresses instead of a routine internal transfer, after which funds were rapidly laundered.
stories.why_it_matters: Audit multi-signature platform integrations and independently verify on-chain transaction details before signing.

stories.headline: Trimera Health discloses breach exposing psychiatric patient records
stories.technical: Trimera Health reported a data breach that occurred between September 24th and 29th, 2026, and was discovered on September 29th, 2026. The incident affected 1,343 individuals, compromising names, addresses, and sensitive medical information. The breach was detailed in a Texas Attorney General data security breach report.
stories.why_it_matters: Check your insurance statements and credit reports for suspicious activity.

stories.headline: Netgear routers hit by multiple CVE vulnerabilities, patches released
stories.technical: Four CVEs – CVE-2026-11732, CVE-2026-11731, CVE-2026-11730, CVE-2026-9218 – allow attackers with local network access to run unauthorised commands or hijack sessions on RAX5, EX3700, CBR40 Orbi and other Netgear devices. Firmware updates are available.
stories.why_it_matters: Patch affected Netgear firmware immediately to stop unauthorised command execution.

stories.headline: Teams help-desk scams escalate into AD CS certificate abuse
stories.technical: Microsoft Threat Intelligence investigated two human-operated intrusions using Teams calls and messages to impersonate IT support and obtain Quick Assist access. Attackers staged Python, Bun or Java runtimes, discovered AD CS, then abused ESC1 templates for privileged certificates and DCSync, or used PetitPotam with ESC8 Web Enrollment and PKINIT. No Teams vulnerability was involved.
stories.why_it_matters: Audit AD CS templates and restrict remote-support access to prevent privileged certificate abuse.

stories.headline: DOJ subpoenas California election officials over voter registration data
stories.technical: The US Department of Justice has issued grand jury subpoenas to California election offices, including Los Angeles County, regarding voter registration administration. The investigation focuses on the removal of 'potential noncitizens' from rolls. The DOJ and DHS are using federal databases and commercially acquired personal information, which state officials and courts have previously criticised as unreliable.
stories.why_it_matters: Monitor legal disputes over federal access and use of state voter registration data.

stories.headline: OWASP launches free RAID-AI ransomware resilience framework
stories.technical: The Ransomware Assessment and Incident Defense Framework for AI Systems (RAID-AI) provides a free web console for manually assessing ransomware controls across general cybersecurity and AI-specific areas, including models, data, tools and runtime. Controls use maturity levels from zero to five and map to NIST CSF 2.0, CISA CPG 2.0, MITRE ATT&CK, MITRE ATLAS and NIST Adversarial.
stories.why_it_matters: Assess AI ransomware controls without connecting systems or uploading sensitive documents.

stories.headline: Researchers struggle to explain Italy’s unusual cyber threat landscape
stories.technical: Researchers report that Italy faces an unusually diverse range of cyber threats, but the excerpt provides no technical detail, affected products, vulnerabilities, threat actors, attack methods or indicators of compromise. The reasons for the country’s distinct threat profile remain unclear.
stories.why_it_matters: Review national threat reporting and prioritise controls relevant to Italian organisations.

stories.headline: FBI Arrests 28 Scam Operators, Seizes $11M in Nigeria, Ghana
stories.technical: The FBI, with UK National Crime Agency and Meta, arrested 28 scam operators across Nigeria and Ghana, seized 356 devices, removed 3.7 million fraudulent social‑media accounts, and traced $11 million in funds. The crackdown identified 117 trafficking victims coerced into running fraud scripts.
stories.why_it_matters: Report suspicious social‑media activity and support victim recovery.

stories.headline: Autoscaling can terminate hosts before IR teams respond
stories.technical: In autoscaled cloud environments, an autoscaling group can terminate an instance within minutes of an alert, erasing forensic artefacts before responders can isolate the host. NIST SP 800‑61 Rev. 3 and CSF 2.0 emphasise continuous detection and analysis, but the forensic window may close before evidence is captured. IR plans must anticipate rapid termination and preserve artefacts in advance.
stories.why_it_matters: Adjust IR plans to account for rapid instance termination in autoscaled environments

stories.headline: Aftermarket Android car head units found containing bloatware and spyware
stories.technical: Reverse engineering of a cheap aftermarket Android automotive head unit using Claude AI revealed pre-installed bloatware and potential spyware. Uncovered components included a voice assistant utilising Android WebView that consumed a third of CPU capacity while idle, alongside Baidu location services, an active call recorder, and unnecessary third-party applications, highlighting IoT security concerns.
stories.why_it_matters: Exercise caution when connecting unbranded aftermarket IoT devices to vehicles or personal networks.

stories.headline: Defense contractor pleads guilty to aiding North Korean remote worker scheme
stories.technical: John Allen Kurrle Jr. admitted using his identity and top-secret clearance to support at least 88 US job applications, producing nine offers. Co-conspirators remotely accessed company laptops hosted at his Virginia home, including one assigned to a generative AI military component project. The company detected an identity mismatch during a video call and terminated the employment before contract work began.
stories.why_it_matters: Review remote-worker identity checks and laptop handling for contractors handling sensitive government work.

Gardaí are investigating theft reports around Watergrasshill and Mitchelstown, with CCTV reportedly showing suspects scouting properties and attempting vehicle access.

stories.headline: Anne Arundel County warns of 2025 cyberattack
stories.technical: Anne Arundel County officials are sending letters to residents affected by a 2025 cyberattack. Details of the attack, including the threat actors and methods used, remain undisclosed.
stories.why_it_matters: Check if you're affected and follow county guidance

stories.headline: Third‑party script breaches highlight runtime risks
stories.technical: Polymarket’s front‑end was compromised when a third‑party vendor injected a malicious script, causing loss of roughly £2.5m. The incident did not affect Polymarket servers but altered code executed in users’ browsers. A separate lawsuit alleges Hims & Hers’ third‑party tracking code sent visitors’ health data to ad platforms. No patch required, but monitoring is advised.
stories.why_it_matters: Check third‑party scripts and monitor vendor security for your web apps

stories.headline: Incomplete SAR responses expose gaps in data discovery
stories.technical: UK GDPR requires controllers to respond to SARs within one month. The article shows a workflow that meets the SLA but misses data in undiscovered stores. It highlights that incomplete discovery can leave personal data unaccounted for, undermining erasure obligations and exposing organisations to regulatory risk and potential penalties for non-compliance in the future regulations.
stories.why_it_matters: Ensure discovery covers all data stores before SAR responses.

stories.headline: Fake GitHub repository targets AI agents with SolanaCry malware
stories.technical: SolanaCry masquerades as a Solana starter kit and instructs AI coding agents to run PowerShell, downloading a 21 MB fileless dropper. It extracts 13 signed NetSupport Manager components plus client32.ini, connects to maxwintodaybtc.com:443, hides notifications, persists through client32.exe in the Windows Run registry key, and clears command history. AIR Research Lab linked the RADIUSSecret signature to eSentire’s EVALUSION cluster, but attribution remains unconfirmed.
stories.why_it_matters: Review AI coding-agent repositories and isolate cryptocurrency wallets from developer workstations.

stories.headline: Patched abandoned app prevents mass machine takeover
stories.technical: A security firm patched a decade-old application after finding that abandoned domains could enable attackers to take over millions of machines. The update closes a takeover path created when the software's original domain lapsed, highlighting the persistent risk of unmaintained projects and lapsed infrastructure.
stories.why_it_matters: Update the application and replace any abandoned domains still used for administration.

stories.headline: WordPress Core RCE flaw hit by nearly 63,000 attack attempts
stories.technical: Unauthenticated attackers targeted a remote code execution vulnerability in WordPress Core versions 4.7 through 7.1.3, carrying a CVSS score of 8.1. The flaw exploits predictable, web-accessible staging paths used during full-package core updates. Attackers must hit a narrow race condition window while the update unpacks. Wordfence blocked 62,969 exploit attempts. Administrators must update to version 7.1.4.
stories.why_it_matters: Update WordPress to version 7.1.4 immediately to prevent remote code execution.

stories.headline: North Korean Hackers Steal Record $6.3B in Binance Breach
stories.technical: Hackers linked to North Korea stole at least $6.3 billion in cryptocurrency from Binance after compromising an engineer's laptop. The breach allowed attackers to access a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions. Binance suspended deposits and withdrawals while investigating the incident, stating no private keys were compromised.
stories.why_it_matters: Check your crypto exchange account security and monitor platform updates.

daily.headline: Lapsus$ teen hacking group claims Okta and Microsoft breaches
daily.technical: Four years ago, the Lapsus$ group posted screenshots claiming they had accessed the identity provider Okta and Microsoft's source code. They used bribed insiders, SIM swaps and MFA fatigue rather than advanced malware to get inside. Several members, including teenagers from the UK, were later arrested.
daily.why_it_matters: Simple social engineering beat some of the world's biggest companies.

daily.headline: Delete accounts you no longer use
daily.technical: Old accounts on forums, shops and apps still hold your details, and often an old reused password. When those sites are breached, your data goes with them. Close what you don't need and change the password on anything you keep.
daily.why_it_matters: Every unused account is a breach waiting to include you.
